steps.text: Combine 6 cups of water, beans, tomatoes, ham, onion, celery, Worcestershire sauce, minced garlic, bouillon, parsley, garlic powder, and bay leaf in a stock pot; bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for two hours.
Add 3 cups of water; stir in salt and pepper. Simmer for an additional two hours. Discard bay leaf before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Navy Bean Soup
raw_recipe.description: This flavorsome navy bean soup is slow-simmered to perfection for a hearty meal chock-full of tomatoes, celery, ham, herbs, and spices.
raw_recipe.name: Navy Bean Soup

Add 3 cups of water; stir in salt and pepper. Simmer for an additional two hours. Discard bay leaf before serving.

review.reviewBody: Here's a tip from my mom. If you are going to use a ham bone for flaver, cook the ham bone in water & make the stock first. Then use it instead of cooking it all together. It will give a lot more room in the pot for veggies & it is a lot easier to remove bone & bits from stock then it is when its in the soup.

With changes below, this warrants five stars.

Okay, I am NOT a purist and use whatever tastes best. White Northern beans I find a little boring, so I used a bulk foods 13 bean mix, which had split peas, lentils, pinto, black, black eyed peas, garbanzo and several other types INCLUDING White Northern. This bean mix is cheaper, especially in bulk, and possesses a much more complex flavor than just white beans alone.

Second, in the six cups of water I used half chicken broth and half vegetable broth (both Better than Boullion) so that the flavors better complimented the vegetable mix in the soup.

Cayenne pepper instead of black, to go with the smoky flavor of half a pack of bacon (as opposed to straight ham, it was all I had on hand).

I added 1 teaspoon celery seed to go with the celery stalks, plus three large carrots. Also, though I had diced tomatoes on hand I figured hand-chopped Roma would add more flavor and better texture.


The beans were soaked overnight, so the soup only needs three hours on high in the crock pot to combine and reduce properly. Served with homemade cornbread it was PHENOMENAL! One of the best bean soups I have had, with the tweaks. Perhaps it is not Navy Bean anymore, but I think the taste is quite a lot better.

So good! After reading the reviews where people liked the smokey flavor of bacon added to the recipe I decided to use kielbasa rather than ham- I love how kielbasa flavors a soup broth! I diced the kielbasa and onion and threw them in the slow cooker with a little oil on high for about an hour. Then I tossed in the rest of the ingredients and turned the heat to low overnight. PERFECT fall recipe. I used a can of Ro*tel instead of regular diced tomatoes and added a can of tomato sauce, 1 Tbsp of Italian Seasoning, 1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp onion powder, 1/2 tsp chile-lime seasoning, and 1/4 tsp cayenne. So ridiculously good!

I made this in a crockpot. I could only get 6 cups of liquid in the pot, so I put in 4 cups of vegetable broth, and 2 cups of water. I put in one tsp Vegetable Better Than bouillon as had no chicken broth. Used no salt at all. Everything else I had, so no more substitutions. Cooked it 8 hours on high, and the beans were still a little under done. Cooked one more hour, and they were perfect. We really liked the soup, but was a bit salty because of the ham. We eat a very low salt diet. I am sure it would be fine for other people.

I combined the best two recommendations on here. Simmered the ham bone from my spiral ham in vegetable broth for an hour. Used a bag of dried 15 beans that I boiled for 10 minuets to soften. Added the ham broth (minus the bone) to the slow cooker with all the ingredients. Followed the rest of the recipe. Cooked on low for the day. Terrific with some fresh bread!!!

This was delicious. I added 1 chopped up carrot Substituted the water with store bought vegetable stock Simmered the soup with 2 smoked ham hocks I Let the soup cool overnight in refrigerator and I skimmed all the fat off the surfave the next day

I’m never losing this recipe, best I’ve ever had, hands down!!! Easy, simmered, FANTASTIC flavor and no overnight soak needed. I followed the recipe except a few teeny, tiny modifications. (Truly, very small) 1. No water, I used clear ham broth (made from our Christmas ham bone) half and half with chicken broth. 2. Added a couple of carrots just because I always do in soup. 3. I didn’t have a bouillon cube, but had Jamison’s ham soup base instead. I used that, 4 tsp, then adjusted to taste. Didn’t need any more salt. 4. Last, as I do with all homemade soups, I put a couple ladlefuls of the beans and stuff (the solids) in a small blender and puréed it with some of the three last cups of liquid added after the first two hours of simmering. We like our soups a little bit creamy and fuller, not thin. This trick always “fills out” the finished soup broth. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND this recipe. Comfort soup in a pot!!!

Best recipe I've found. Everyone in my family really loves it. What I do is use chicken stock instead of water and still add the boullion cube. I also chop up baby carrots on the thick side (because they will cook down). I put the ham bone in from the start and scrap off meat every time I stir it. I don't presoak or cook the beans before starting. 

You can't go wrong with this recipe if you like navy bean soup. Thanks for sharing.

I come from four generations of soup makers. And that’s just when they started counting. This soup is delicious, full-bodied and flavorful. Like just about everyone else I added my own tweaks: I soaked the beans overnight; I boiled ham hocks, using the resulting broth as stock for my soup; I did not add chicken boullion, instead adding smoke flavoring - about 1 tablespoon. Lastly, I cooked my soup in my Instant Pot.

Loved it, but I altered the recipe slightly to be vegan. Omitted ham, pepper, bouillon. 2 cloves garlic instead of 1 and 1 t garlic salt instead of 2. 1 can Ro-Tel original 284 ml instead of stewed tomatoes. 946ml container vegetable broth (don’t add salt if broth has it) and 1 cup water instead of 6 cups water. Add 1 t thyme and 1 t cumin. After soaking beans overnight, I only needed to simmer 1.5 hours.

New Years day tradition! Excellent with a few tweaks mentioned above, I cooked the Christmas Ham bone in Vegetable broth, added the half & half and traded the diced tomato for Rotel (extra zing to ring in the new year!) My mom always added a bit of ketchup to her bowl and I like it that way -although the rest of my family thinks I'm nuts. Dont knock it until you've tried it ;-) Here's to a great 2025!!
Loved this recipe. I added carrots and a little bit of chopped bacon. My husband loved it too!!

Not a fan of adding tomatoes and used 1/2 an onion. I also add dumplings made from Bisquick. 1 cup Bisquick + 1/3 cup of milk. Add dough in small tablespoons. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes and covered for 10 minutes. Dumplings add a little extra!!

In my family we call this Coast Guard bean soup lol! Only thing I do not use a bouillon cube I add a can of bone broth or stock.sometimes I add liquid smoke a couple of dashes otherwise this is a good base to build on and use up that extra ham!
NO CHANGES
I substituted pork for chicken nice

This was really tasty. I did substitute a roasted chicken for ham. I also cooked the onion and garlic first so there wasn't a big harsh flavor of onion and garlic in the soup. I didn't have bullion cubes so I used up my better than bullion and some bullion powder. I think I ended up using the equivalent of three cubes. At the end, about an hour before the soup was finished, I did taste the broth to see if it needed anything, and for my family's tastes we added two tablespoons of apple cider vinegar and that really added nice acidity. I think this is a very versatile recipe and you could add all kinds of veggies, carrots come to mind, would be a nice addition to add a few more veggies. Overall my family was very happy with the soup, even my spouse who only likes spicy food. He said he would have added a splash of Sriracha. I didn't do that because the rest of our family can't tolerate as much spice as he can. My son added a hefty slice of crusty sourdough to dip in the broth. This soup was nice and filling without making you over full. Would happily make this again.
This is my recipe as well forever, I just add a rue first and tomatoe sauce, potatoes, and a few sweet potatoes, everything else is the same
Easy and flavorful. I added cayenne peppers just a dash! Perfecto. I also used a 16 bean mix and I liked it better. Thanks for the recipe
I doubled the bullion cube and cut down on one cup of water. But this is excellent and so easy to put together and so inexpensive. I also added sliced carrots because my wife loves them in bean soup
